note.explanation: Entrepreneurship means starting a business or organisation and developing ideas into useful products or services. Digital tools help entrepreneurs understand customers, promote products and sell to people online. A business plan explains how a business will operate and earn income.
examples: A student can use an online survey to find out which books local students need, then sell those books through an online bookstore.
A farmer-focused business could use design thinking to learn farmers’ problems and test a simple service before launching it.
note.checkAnswer: Market analysis is the study of customers, their needs and competitors.
note.simple: Find a real need, plan a useful solution, and use suitable tools to reach customers.
note.checkQuestion: What does market analysis help a business understand?
note.title: Planning a Digital Business
steps: Identify a customer need using research, surveys or observation.
Develop a useful idea and improve it by understanding the users.
Plan the market, income, costs and strategies in a business plan.
Use digital tools to promote and sell the product or service.
Consider how the business can support social, environmental and economic sustainability.
note.answer: A business plan describes the market, customers, business strategies and ways the business will earn revenue.

options: The process of starting a new business or organization
The process of buying and selling stocks
The process of working for a large company
The process of creating a marketing campaign
rationales: Correct: entrepreneurship involves starting a new business or organization.
Buying and selling stocks is not the meaning of entrepreneurship.
Working for a large company does not itself mean starting a business.
Creating a marketing campaign can be one business activity, but it is not entrepreneurship's meaning.

mcqs.stem: Q12.2. What is a key characteristic of entrepreneurs?
rationales: Entrepreneurs do not simply avoid all risks; they assess and take suitable risks.
Seeking job security is not the key characteristic asked for here.
Correct: innovation means introducing new ideas or ways of doing things.
Entrepreneurs may improve or change established methods rather than only follow them.

mcqs.stem: Q12.3. What is an example of a digital technology used by modern entrepreneurs?
rationales: Newspaper advertisements are a traditional, printed medium.
Television commercials are not the digital technology example intended here.
Correct: mobile apps are digital technologies used by modern entrepreneurs.
Door-to-door sales is a sales method, not a digital technology.

mcqs.stem: Q12.4. Which of the following is an example of a digital tool for creating and editing documents online?
rationales: SurveyMonkey is mainly used to create surveys.
Correct: Google Docs is used to create and edit documents online.
SEMrush is a digital marketing and search engine tool.
Zendesk is a customer service platform.

mcqs.stem: Q12.5. Which tool is commonly used for optimizing website content for search engines?
rationales: Hootsuite is used to manage social media.
Correct: Yoast SEO helps optimize website content for search engines.
Shopify is an e-commerce platform for online stores.
PayPal is a digital payment service.

mcqs.stem: Q12.6. Which of the following is NOT a technique for identifying market needs?
rationales: Surveys and questionnaires can collect information about customer needs.
Market research can identify customers and their needs.
Observation can reveal customer behaviour and problems.
Correct according to the answer key: brainstorming generates ideas, while the other listed options directly gather evidence about market needs.

mcqs.stem: Q12.7. What is the first step in the design thinking process?
rationales: Prototyping comes later, after a problem and possible solution have been explored.
Testing takes place after a prototype has been made.
Correct: empathizing begins by understanding the users and their needs.
Defining follows the work of understanding users.

mcqs.stem: Q12.8. What is the primary purpose of creating a business plan?
rationales: Correct according to the answer key: a business plan can present the business clearly to attract investors.
A plan may outline growth strategies, but this is not the keyed primary purpose in this question.
Studying market trends is part of planning, not the main purpose of the whole plan.
Digital marketing strategies can be included in a plan, but they are only one part of it.

options: Researching competitors and understanding customer needs
mcqs.stem: Q12.9. What does market analysis involve?
rationales: Revenue forecasts are a financial planning activity, not the main market analysis described here.
Correct: market analysis researches competitors and helps understand customer needs.
Pricing strategies may use market information but are not the definition of market analysis.
Digital marketing campaigns are implemented after planning and are not market analysis itself.

mcqs.stem: Q12.10. Which Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) focuses on affordable and clean energy?
rationales: SDG5 focuses on gender equality.
Correct: SDG7 focuses on affordable and clean energy.
SDG12 focuses on responsible consumption and production.
SDG17 focuses on partnerships for the goals.

written.text: Q12.1. What is the meaning of the word entrepreneur and its origin?
written.finalAnswer: An entrepreneur is a person who starts and manages a business, taking risks to develop an idea. The word comes from the French word entreprendre, meaning “to undertake.”

rubric.why: The meaning of entrepreneur is required.
rubric.description: Explain what an entrepreneur does.
rubric.how: State that an entrepreneur starts or manages a business.

rubric.why: The question also asks for the word's origin.
rubric.description: Give the origin and meaning of the original word.
rubric.how: Name the French origin entreprendre and its meaning, “to undertake.”

modelAnswer: An entrepreneur is a person who starts and manages a business, taking risks to develop an idea.
The word comes from the French word entreprendre, meaning “to undertake.”

written.text: Q12.2. How do digital technologies help entrepreneurs reach a global audience?
written.finalAnswer: Digital technologies let entrepreneurs promote and sell products online to customers in many places, communicate with them and receive orders beyond their local area.

rubric.why: The answer must explain the role of digital technology.
rubric.description: Identify online promotion or selling.
rubric.how: Explain that digital tools let a business promote or sell online.

rubric.why: The question asks how entrepreneurs can reach a global audience.
rubric.description: Explain the wider reach beyond local customers.
rubric.how: State that online access can reach customers in different places.

modelAnswer: Digital technologies let entrepreneurs promote and sell products online to customers in many places.
They can communicate with customers and receive orders beyond their local area.

written.text: Q12.3. What is an e-commerce platform, and why is it important for businesses?
written.finalAnswer: An e-commerce platform is a digital platform for displaying and selling products or services online. It is important because it helps a business reach customers and receive orders over the internet.

rubric.why: The answer must define an e-commerce platform.
rubric.description: Describe it as a platform for online selling.
rubric.how: State that it displays or sells products or services online.

rubric.why: The question asks why the platform matters to a business.
rubric.description: Give a business benefit.
rubric.how: Explain that it helps reach customers or receive online orders.

modelAnswer: An e-commerce platform is a digital platform for displaying and selling products or services online.
It helps a business reach customers and receive orders over the internet.

written.text: Q12.4. Why is it important to identify market needs when generating a business idea?
written.finalAnswer: Identifying market needs helps an entrepreneur create a product or service that solves a real customer problem and has people who may want to buy it.

rubric.why: The answer should connect the business idea to customers' real needs.
rubric.description: Identify the need to understand customers.
rubric.how: State that research reveals what customers need or want.

rubric.why: A business idea should be useful and have potential customers.
rubric.description: Explain the benefit of meeting a real need.
rubric.how: Say the idea can solve a problem or attract buyers.

modelAnswer: Identifying market needs helps an entrepreneur understand customers' problems and wants.
The entrepreneur can then create a useful product or service that people may want to buy.

written.text: Q12.5. What is the main purpose of using design thinking in creative problem-solving?
written.finalAnswer: Design thinking helps create practical, creative solutions by understanding users and their needs, then developing and improving possible solutions.

rubric.why: Design thinking starts by focusing on the people who will use the solution.
rubric.description: Mention understanding users.
rubric.how: Explain that it identifies users' needs or problems.

rubric.why: The purpose is to develop useful responses to the problem.
rubric.description: Explain the goal of the process.
rubric.how: State that it helps create or improve practical solutions.

modelAnswer: Design thinking helps solve problems by first understanding the users and their needs.
It then supports the development and improvement of creative, practical solutions.

written.text: Q12.6. Explain the importance of market analysis in a business plan. Give an example relevant to a local business in Pakistan.
written.finalAnswer: Market analysis helps a business understand its customers, their needs and its competitors, so it can plan suitable products and strategies. For example, a Lahore bakery could study local customers’ preferences and nearby bakeries before choosing what to sell and how to price it.

rubric.why: Market analysis identifies the customers and competition relevant to the plan.
rubric.description: Explain the function of market analysis.
rubric.how: Mention understanding customers, needs or competitors.

rubric.why: The question requires a relevant local example.
rubric.description: Give a Pakistani business example.
rubric.how: Name a local business and show what it could investigate.

modelAnswer: Market analysis helps a business understand customers, their needs and competitors so it can plan suitable products and strategies.
For example, a Lahore bakery could study local preferences and nearby bakeries before choosing products and prices.

written.text: Q12.7. What are revenue models, and why are they essential components of a business plan?
written.finalAnswer: Revenue models explain how a business will earn money, for example by selling products or charging for services. They are essential because they show how the business expects to generate income and support its costs.

rubric.why: The answer must define a revenue model.
rubric.description: Explain how a revenue model describes income.
rubric.how: State that it shows how the business earns money.

rubric.why: The question asks why revenue models are essential.
rubric.description: Explain their importance for planning.
rubric.how: Connect the model to income, costs or the business plan.

modelAnswer: Revenue models explain how a business will earn money, for example by selling products or charging for services.
They are essential because they show how the business expects to generate income and support its costs.

written.text: Q12.8. How can businesses contribute to environmental sustainability according to the Sustainable Development Goals?
written.finalAnswer: Businesses can support environmental sustainability by using resources responsibly, reducing waste and pollution, and supporting goals such as affordable and clean energy (SDG7) and responsible consumption and production (SDG12).

rubric.why: The answer should describe an environmental action by a business.
rubric.description: Give a practical way to reduce environmental harm.
rubric.how: Mention responsible resource use, waste reduction or reducing pollution.

rubric.why: The question specifically refers to the Sustainable Development Goals.
rubric.description: Connect the action to an SDG.
rubric.how: Name a relevant goal, such as SDG7 or SDG12.

modelAnswer: Businesses can use resources responsibly and reduce waste and pollution.
They can support SDG7 by using clean energy and SDG12 through responsible consumption and production.

written.text: Q12.1. Explain why entrepreneurship is important for economic growth and innovation. Provide examples from the text to support your answer.
written.finalAnswer: Entrepreneurship supports economic growth by creating businesses, jobs and income. Entrepreneurs introduce innovative products and services, use digital technologies to reach customers, and can respond to market needs. For example, an online business using mobile apps or an e-commerce platform can sell to customers beyond its local area. These activities encourage competition, improve services and contribute to the economy.

rubric.why: Economic contribution is a central part of the question.
rubric.description: Explain how entrepreneurship supports the economy.
rubric.how: Link new businesses to jobs, income or economic activity.

rubric.why: The question also asks about innovation.
rubric.description: Explain how entrepreneurs develop or improve ideas.
rubric.how: Describe new or improved products and services.

rubric.why: The answer must support its explanation with a relevant example.
rubric.description: Give a digital entrepreneurship example.
rubric.how: Explain how a digital tool or platform helps a business reach customers.

rubric.why: A full answer connects entrepreneurship to wider benefits and ends with a supported conclusion.
rubric.description: Show another benefit and conclude clearly.
rubric.how: Connect the business to customer needs, improved services or competition.

modelAnswer: Entrepreneurship supports economic growth by creating businesses, jobs and income.
Entrepreneurs introduce innovative products and services and respond to market needs.
Digital technologies, such as mobile apps and e-commerce platforms, can help entrepreneurs reach customers beyond their local area.
For example, an online business can sell to more customers and compete by offering useful products or services.
This creates economic activity, encourages innovation and can improve the choices available to customers.

written.text: Q12.2. Explain how market research tools, online marketing tools, and e-commerce platforms can work together to help a business succeed in the digital world.
written.finalAnswer: Market research tools such as surveys help a business understand customer needs and competitors. Online marketing tools can then promote suitable products to those customers. An e-commerce platform displays the products, accepts orders and supports online selling. Used together, these tools help a business make informed choices, reach customers and turn interest into sales.

rubric.why: Market research provides information for business decisions.
rubric.description: Explain the research tools and what they reveal.
rubric.how: Name a research tool and link it to customer needs or competitors.

rubric.why: The answer needs to explain how the business attracts its audience.
rubric.description: Explain the role of online marketing.
rubric.how: State how digital marketing promotes products to customers.

rubric.why: The e-commerce platform is another required part of the explanation.
rubric.description: Explain what the platform enables.
rubric.how: Show how customers can view products or place orders online.

rubric.why: The question asks how the tools work together to support success.
rubric.description: Connect research, promotion and selling.
rubric.how: Explain the sequence from understanding customers to reaching them and receiving sales.

modelAnswer: Market research tools, such as surveys, help a business understand customer needs and competitors.
The business can use this information to choose products that are suitable for its customers.
Online marketing tools can then promote those products to the intended audience.
An e-commerce platform displays the products and allows customers to place orders online.
Together, research guides the business, marketing attracts customers and e-commerce supports online sales.

written.text: Q12.3. Explain the design thinking process and how it can be applied to create a new product or service. Provide an example of how design thinking could be used to help farmers in rural Pakistan.
written.finalAnswer: Design thinking begins with empathizing to understand users, followed by defining their problem, generating ideas, making a prototype and testing it. To help farmers in rural Pakistan, a team could speak with farmers about difficulties obtaining weather or crop information, define the main problem, develop ideas for a simple mobile service, create a basic prototype and test it with farmers. Their feedback would guide improvements before the service is launched.

rubric.why: The process starts by understanding the people affected.
rubric.description: Explain the first step and identify the users.
rubric.how: Describe empathizing with users and their needs.

rubric.why: The problem must be clearly stated before useful ideas can be chosen.
rubric.description: Explain defining the issue and generating ideas.
rubric.how: Mention defining the problem and considering possible solutions.

rubric.why: Prototyping and testing make the proposed solution practical and improvable.
rubric.description: Explain how a solution is developed and checked.
rubric.how: Describe making a prototype, testing it and using feedback.

rubric.why: The answer must apply the process to the requested local example.
rubric.description: Give a relevant farmer-focused application.
rubric.how: Describe a practical service for rural farmers and how they would test it.

modelAnswer: Design thinking begins with empathizing to understand the users and their needs.
The next step is defining the problem clearly and then developing possible ideas.
A prototype is made and tested with users so that their feedback can improve the solution.
For farmers in rural Pakistan, a team could first ask farmers about difficulties in getting weather or crop information.
The team could define this as the problem and consider a simple mobile service that provides useful information.
It could create a basic prototype and test it with farmers in the area.
Farmers' feedback would help the team improve the service before launching it.

written.text:
Q12.4. Imagine you want to start a small online bookstore catering to students in your area. Develop a comprehensive business plan for your bookstore, including.  
(a) A market analysis focusing on student reading habits and competitors.  
(b) A revenue model outlining how you will generate income.  
(c) Digital marketing strategies you will use to promote your bookstore online.
written.finalAnswer: The plan would research students’ reading habits, preferred subjects, budgets and book-buying methods, and compare local bookshops and online sellers. The bookstore could earn revenue by selling new and second-hand textbooks, exam guides and other books, with income from each sale and possibly delivery charges. It could promote its books through social media posts, student groups, a simple website and online offers. An e-commerce platform or online ordering system could display stock and receive orders, while reliable local delivery would serve students in the area.

rubric.why: The question explicitly requires market analysis of students and competitors.
rubric.description: Analyse customers and competing sellers.
rubric.how: Discuss student preferences and identify competitors such as local bookshops or online sellers.

rubric.why: The plan must explain how the bookstore earns money.
rubric.description: Describe a suitable revenue model.
rubric.how: State what books are sold and how sales or charges generate income.

rubric.why: Promotion strategies are specifically requested.
rubric.description: Give practical online marketing strategies.
rubric.how: Name and explain suitable online promotion methods.

rubric.why: A comprehensive plan should be practical for the local student market.
rubric.description: Show how the business will serve its customers.
rubric.how: Include online ordering, suitable stock or local delivery.

modelAnswer: Business idea: Start an online bookstore for students in the local area, offering textbooks, exam guides and other useful books.
Market analysis: Ask students about their reading habits, subjects, preferred books, budgets and how they buy books.
Compare local bookshops and online sellers by checking their prices, book range and delivery services.
Revenue model: Earn income by selling new and second-hand books, textbooks and exam guides.
The bookstore could also charge a reasonable delivery fee where appropriate.
Digital marketing: Promote available books and offers through social media posts and student groups.
Use a simple website or e-commerce platform to show the stock and receive online orders.
Arrange reliable local delivery so that students in the area can receive their books conveniently.

written.text: Q12.5. Ensure your answers are detailed and include practical examples relevant to starting your bookstore in Pakistan.
written.finalAnswer: Answers should explain each part in detail and use practical examples, such as researching local students’ book needs, comparing nearby bookshops, selling textbooks and exam guides online, promoting through student social media groups, and arranging local delivery in Pakistan.

rubric.why: The prompt asks for detailed answers rather than brief statements.
rubric.description: Develop the explanation.
rubric.how: Address the relevant parts with clear supporting details.

rubric.why: Examples should relate to the proposed student bookstore.
rubric.description: Give a practical bookstore example.
rubric.how: Mention student needs or suitable books for sale.

rubric.why: The examples must fit the Pakistani local context.
rubric.description: Make the examples relevant to the location.
rubric.how: Refer to local customers, competitors or the Pakistani setting.

rubric.why: Practical digital business actions make the answer useful and complete.
rubric.description: Add workable promotion or service examples.
rubric.how: Include online promotion, ordering or local delivery.

modelAnswer: A detailed answer should explain each part of the bookstore plan and support it with practical examples.
For example, research local students' book needs and compare prices and services at nearby bookshops.
The bookstore could sell textbooks and exam guides through an online ordering system.
It could promote books through social media and student groups and arrange local delivery in Pakistan.

written.text: Q12.6. Choose a local business in Pakistan and discuss how it aligns with one or more Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Include its impact on social, environmental, and economic sustainability.
written.finalAnswer: A local solar-panel installation business in Pakistan can support SDG7, affordable and clean energy, by helping homes and businesses use solar power. Socially, it can improve access to electricity and create jobs for trained workers. Environmentally, solar power can reduce reliance on fossil fuels and associated pollution. Economically, the business earns income, employs people and may help customers reduce electricity costs over time.

rubric.why: The answer must select and describe a business relevant to Pakistan.
rubric.description: Identify a suitable local business.
rubric.how: Name a local business and explain its activity.

rubric.why: The business must be linked to at least one SDG.
rubric.description: Name and explain an aligned goal.
rubric.how: Connect the business's work to a relevant SDG.

rubric.why: The question specifically asks for social sustainability impact.
rubric.description: Explain a social effect.
rubric.how: Describe benefits to people, access or employment.

rubric.why: Environmental and economic effects complete the requested discussion.
rubric.description: Explain both environmental and economic impacts.
rubric.how: Describe an environmental benefit and an economic contribution.

modelAnswer: A local solar-panel installation business in Pakistan can align with SDG7, which focuses on affordable and clean energy.
Socially, it can help homes and businesses access electricity and create jobs for trained workers.
Environmentally, solar power can reduce reliance on fossil fuels and the pollution associated with them.
Economically, the business earns income and employs people, while customers may reduce electricity costs over time.
This example shows how a business can support social, environmental and economic sustainability.

examTips: Short questions may ask for a definition, a reason or a local example; give the direct point first and add a clear explanation.
For long questions, use headings or clearly separated paragraphs to cover every part of the question.
For business plans, include customers and competitors, a way to earn revenue, and practical promotion strategies.
For design thinking questions, describe the steps in order and apply each step to the example given.
For SDG questions, name the goal and explain the social, environmental and economic effects separately.

explain.title: Entrepreneurship and innovation
explain.body: Entrepreneurs start businesses and turn ideas into products or services. Their work can create jobs, income and new choices for customers.

explain.title: Digital business tools
explain.body: Digital technologies help businesses communicate, promote and sell beyond their local area. E-commerce platforms make it possible to display products and receive online orders.

explain.title: Understand the market
explain.body: Market analysis helps a business learn about customers, their needs and competitors. Research helps entrepreneurs make better decisions about what to offer.

explain.title: Design thinking
explain.body: Design thinking starts by understanding users and defining their problem. Ideas are developed, made into prototypes and tested so that feedback can improve the solution.

explain.title: Plan income and sustainability
explain.body: A business plan sets out how a business will operate and earn money. Businesses can also support sustainability by using resources responsibly and aligning with relevant SDGs.

mistakes: Do not confuse an entrepreneur with someone who only works for a company; entrepreneurship involves starting or developing a business.
Do not describe market analysis only as calculating income; include customers and competitors.
Do not leave out how the business will earn money when writing a business plan.
Do not list design thinking steps without applying them to the users and problem in the question.
For an SDG answer, name the goal and explain the actual social, environmental and economic impacts.
